e-5087.knowledge_point: Finding the Cartesian Equation of a Curve Defined Parametrically
e-5087.problem:
Find the Cartesian equation of the curve defined parametrically by

$$
x=2t^2, \,\,\, y=t^2+1, \quad t \geq 0.
$$
e-5087.worked_solution:
To find the Cartesian equation, we eliminate $t.$ First we use the $x$ equation to solve for $t^2\mathbin{:}$

$$
x=2t^2 \quad \Rightarrow\quad  t^2 = \dfrac{x}{2}
$$

Now substituting $t^2=\dfrac{x}{2}$ into our expression for $y,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}y & ={t}^{2}+1 \\  & =\frac{x}{2}+1 \\  & =\frac{1}{2}x+1.\end{aligned}
$$

So the Cartesian equation of the given curve is $y=\dfrac{1}{2}x+1.$

Finally, since $t \geq0$ and $x=2t^2,$ we must have $x \geq 0.$

So, the complete Cartesian equation is

$$
y=\dfrac{1}{2}x+1, \quad x \geq 0 .
$$

after.worked_solution:
To find the Cartesian equation, we eliminate $t.$ First, we use the $x$ equation to solve for $t:$

$$
\begin{aligned}x=\sqrt{\,t+1\,}\,⇒\,t={x}^{2}-1\end{aligned}
$$

Now, substituting $t={x}^{2}-1$ into our expression for $y,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}y & =({x}^{2}-1)(4-({x}^{2}-1)) \\  & =({x}^{2}-1)(5-{x}^{2})\end{aligned}
$$

So, the Cartesian equation of the given curve is $y=({x}^{2}-1)(5-{x}^{2}).$

Finally, since $t\ge 0$ and $t={x}^{2}-1,$ we must have ${x}^{2}-1\ge 0,$ i.e., $x\ge 1.$

Therefore, the complete Cartesian equation is $y=({x}^{2}-1)(5-{x}^{2}),\,x\ge 1.$

after.name: Question 3
after.problem:
Find the Cartesian equation of the curve defined parametrically by

$$
x=\frac{t-5}{2},\,\,\,y=({t}^{2}-25)(t-4),\,t\in (-\infty ,\infty ).
$$
after.worked_solution:
To find the Cartesian equation, we eliminate $t.$ First, we use the $x$ equation to solve for $t:$

$$
\begin{aligned}x=\frac{t-5}{2}\,⇒\,t=2x+5\end{aligned}
$$

Now, substituting $t=2x+5$ into our expression for $y,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}y & =((2x+5)^{2}-25)(2x+5-4) \\  & =(4{x}^{2}+20x+25-25)(2x+1) \\  & =(4{x}^{2}+20x)(2x+1) \\  & =4x(x+5)(2x+1).\end{aligned}
$$

So the Cartesian equation of the given curve is $y=4x(x+5)(2x+1).$

EXPLANATION

To find the Cartesian equation, we eliminate t. First, we use the x equation to solve for t: x=t−52⇒t=2x+5

Now, substituting t=2x+5 into our expression for y, we get y=((2x+5)2−25)(2x+5−4)=(4x2+20x+25−25)(2x+1)=(4x2+20x)(2x+1)=4x(x+5)(2x+1).

content.knowledge_point: Finding the Cartesian Equation of a Curve Defined Parametrically
content.problem:
Find the Cartesian equation of the curve defined parametrically by

$$
x=\frac{t-5}{2},\,\,\,y=({t}^{2}-25)(t-4),\,t\in (-\infty ,\infty ).
$$
content.worked_solution:
To find the Cartesian equation, we eliminate $t.$ First, we use the $x$ equation to solve for $t:$

$$
\begin{aligned}x=\frac{t-5}{2}\,⇒\,t=2x+5\end{aligned}
$$

Now, substituting $t=2x+5$ into our expression for $y,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}y & =((2x+5)^{2}-25)(2x+5-4) \\  & =(4{x}^{2}+20x+25-25)(2x+1) \\  & =(4{x}^{2}+20x)(2x+1) \\  & =4x(x+5)(2x+1).\end{aligned}
$$

So the Cartesian equation of the given curve is $y=4x(x+5)(2x+1).$
